events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body: The driver cancelled and asserted a rider no-show, so the fee can only stand through NS-0's driver-cancellation branch and NS-1 [F3][F12][NS-0][NS-1]. All three NS-1 requirements fail on the platform's own records: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:05:55 while 601 m from the pickup point and spent 0 s inside the 200 m radius afterwards, and his closest approach over the whole trip was 545 m — the platform never recorded him at the pickup point [F5][F1][F4][NS-1]. E-mailing "I'm here already … please come out" at 12:06 and claiming a 3-minute wait does not cure this: system records (gps / timeline) override statements (chat / driver statement), and the rider's reply shows she was actually at the pickup point and saw no car [F8][F9][F12][NS-1]. With NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) unmet, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee to be refunded in full; the amount is the cancellation fee on record, $6.61, and on RydeX (non-metered) no extra distance-based computation applies [F6][F3][NS-2][RD-2]. The trace also marks NS-2's second limb: the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS showed him well outside the pickup radius, which Ryde treats as abuse of the arrival/waiting button, so the ruling carries flag_account; RD-6 is not applied since no route deviation is at issue here and the profile alone cannot decide anything [F5][F1][F17][NS-2][RD-6]. The safety screen found no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation: the three chat messages are only an arrival claim, a "where are you?" query and a cancellation notice, the driver's statement is a bare no-show claim, and the complaint is a billing complaint [F8][F9][F10][F11][F12][F14][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].
